specs.why:
RULING B, quoted: "gate the +500 on the Starstone die itself being part of the KEPT AND SCORED selection that bank, not on the player banking anything at all while merely owning one... as a side effect, makes it properly suppressible by Still Waters for the first time".

WHAT THE CODE DOES TODAY. handleBank (~25541) runs `G.matchDice.filter(m => m === 'starstone').length * 500` and adds it to `total`. G.matchDice is the loadout material-id array. It is never asked whether a Starstone was rolled, kept, scored, or even present on the table. Any bank of any size pays. `starstone_bonus` is declared as a die effect at lines 11812 (corvus_ledger_d, amount 300) and 11913 (starstone, amount 500), but grep shows the mechanic string is READ NOWHERE - scoreRoll's `dieEff` never tests it. The loadout filter in handleBank is the entire implementation.

WHAT "KEPT AND SCORED" IS IN THIS CODE - the investigation asked for.

1. G.kept rows. Pushed at four sites: handleRoll's commit (~23382), handleBank's commit (~25094), handleBank's Break-then-bank commit (~25071), and the synthetic BREAK_TRIGGERS rows (17612 obsidian, 17664 vagabond) which carry `vals:[], dice:[]`. Row shape is `{vals, mat, pts, cursed, dice:[{val,mat}]}`.

2. A kept row does NOT record die objects. `dice` is `{val, mat}` only - no `ench`, no `lane`. This is decisive: `_famHushed(d)` is `!!(d && d.ench && _stillWaters())`, so a row can never be asked about Still Waters. Any design that defers the decision to bank time is structurally unable to be suppressed, which is the same reason the ruling says the old wording broke it. THE DECISION MUST BE MADE AT COMMIT TIME, where the pool die objects (`{val, mat, ench, sel, committed, el, lane}`, built at 23479 / 23575 / 24769) are still in hand.

3. Scored vs merely committed. `_splitIcons(selDice)` (17514) splits a selection into `.icons` (dice where `_dieIsIcon(d)`: the die is branded AND showing its brand face) and `.rest`. Only `.rest` reaches the scoring engine; an icon banks zero and fires its brand instead. But the three pushes stamp `dice: selDice.map(...)` / `selD.map(...)` - the WHOLE selection, icons included. So `k.dice` would pay for an icon-face Starstone in a mixed keep, which the ruling forbids. `.rest` is the right set, and it is already the file's own definition of "the dice that scored": `_applyCommitBonuses(_scoreDice, ...)` / `_applyCommitBonuses(_bkScore, ...)` pay Vanguard, Sequence, Flanks, Hot Hand, Perfect Storm and the rest off exactly that array.

MECHANISM CHOSEN. New helper `_starstonePay(dice)` placed immediately after `_dieEffect`, summing `_dieEffect(d).amount` over dice whose effect mechanic is `starstone_bonus`. Each of the three real commit sites stamps `ss:_starstonePay(<scored half>)` onto the row it pushes. handleBank replaces the loadout filter with `(G.kept||[]).reduce((a,k) => a + (k.ss||0), 0)`.

WHY THIS SHAPE. (a) It is decided where the die objects live, so it can see ench. (b) Carrying the answer on G.kept means zero new lifetime to manage - G.kept is already cleared at turn start (22945) and on every bust path, so a bust pays nothing and no new flag needs resetting anywhere. A standalone `G._ssPot` counter would have needed a reset added to each of those paths and would rot the first time a new bust path appeared. (c) The synthetic Break rows push `dice:[]` and no `ss`, so a shatter cannot conjure a payout - correct by construction rather than by a special case.

STILL WATERS COMES FREE, AND YES, ROUTING BUYS IT. `_starstonePay` calls `_dieEffect`, which calls `_famHushed`, which returns true for a WORKED die (`d.ench` set) while `_ruleActive('confession','p')` holds; `_dieEffect` then returns null and the die contributes 0. No suppression check is written into the new code. This is the first time the trait is reachable at all: the old loadout filter walked bare material ids, precisely the gap `_famHushed`'s own comment already names for Brass and the shield. Note the existing claim at ~17585 that "scoreRoll's own dieEff asks the same question inline - so the scoring traits (Jade wilds, Amber triples, Starstone bank) are hushed too" is FALSE for Starstone today, because scoreRoll never reads `starstone_bonus`; after this patch the claim becomes true by a different route.

The Break-then-bank push at ~25071 is a genuinely distinct row, not a duplicate: it pushes, sets `G._breakThenBank`, and `_breakBegin` returns before the second push is reached, so skipping it would silently drop the bonus on that path.

1. CORVUS'S LEDGER GOES LIVE - the one deliberate scope decision, flag it to the reviewer. Driving off `mechanic === 'starstone_bonus'` rather than `mat === 'starstone'` means corvus_ledger_d (line 11812, amount 300) starts paying 300 per qualifying bank. It pays NOTHING today: grep confirms the mechanic string is read nowhere, so the existing comment at ~25613 - "the +300 rides the starstone_bonus mechanic in scoring" - is simply false, and its desc "Every bank +300" has never been true. Routing by mechanic is the principled family-effect path the ruling asks for and it repairs a lie already in the file, but it IS an unmeasured buff to a boss relic in a balance pass. To scope the patch strictly to Starstone, change one clause in _starstonePay to `if(e&&e.mechanic==='starstone_bonus'&&d.mat==='starstone')` and drop the last paragraph of its comment. I recommend keeping it as specified and noting the relic in the changelog; the ruling text does not address it either way.

2. HOT DICE CAN PAY THE SAME DIE TWICE. The ruling says "part of the KEPT AND SCORED selection that bank" and does not say per die per bank. If a Starstone is kept and scored, hot dice clears the row, and the same lane's Starstone is kept and scored again in the same turn, the bank pays 1000 for one die. I implemented PER PARTICIPATION, matching how Amber's triple bonus and the per-commit card bonuses pay. Capping it is possible - pool dice carry `lane`, so the rows could dedupe by lane - but that needs `lane` added to the stamp and a cross-row pass, and I did not want to invent a rule the brief does not state. If the intended reading is "at most once per die per bank", say so and I will respec. Note this is the only case where the new rule can pay MORE than the old one; everywhere else it is a strict nerf.

3. "SCORED" IS DEFINED AS THE NON-ICON HALF, NOT AS scoreRoll's `used` ARRAY. With a consume-extras card live (Bookends, Twin Fury, Sevens Gift, Lucky Seven, The Ladder, Ascending) scoreSelection relaxes its all-dice-must-be-used check, so a genuinely unused leftover die can ride along in `_scoreDice` and would pay. I chose the same set `_applyCommitBonuses` uses so Starstone is consistent with every other per-commit bonus rather than uniquely stricter. Residual gap, deliberately taken; worth its own ruling if the leftover case matters.

4. NPC SIDE LEFT ON OWNERSHIP. finOpp (~27338) still pays `G.matchOppDice.filter(m === 'starstone').length * 500` on any NPC bank. specs.why:
RULING: "Break cannot target a borrowed die at all, full stop... a borrowed die is simply an ILLEGAL BREAK TARGET, same shape as a Preserved die being illegal", and "This is specifically about DELIBERATE Break targeting - passive/natural death on a borrowed die (Obsidian's own shatter) is UNCHANGED."

WHAT THE CODE DOES TODAY. `_breakBegin` (fark_proto.html:17706) builds its target list as `G.pool.filter(function(d){return !d.committed&&d!==src&&!_breakPreserved(d);})`, then outlines each survivor with `.break-target` and binds `d.el.onclick=function(){_breakDie(d);}`. Exclusion is expressed as ONE named predicate, `_breakPreserved(d)` (17694), applied twice: once in that filter, once again inside `_breakDie` (17879) at the point of no return, where it famLogs and returns while still armed. Nothing anywhere consults `G._fairTrade` on the Break path, so a borrowed die is a fully legal target today.

THE LOAN STATE. `CFX.fair_trade.use` (12400) writes `G._fairTrade={lane:worst,was:G.matchDice[worst],borrowed:inv[best]}` and then `G.matchDice[worst]=inv[best]`. So `borrowed` is the stash die that came IN and now stands in lane `ft.lane`; `was` is the player's own die, benched, still owned. Pool dice are stamped with their seat at creation (`const _lane=(G.pool.length+i)%G.matchDice.length; const mat=G.matchDice[_lane]`), and `_laneOf(d)` reads that stamp - the identical hook `_breakPreserved` already uses for its lane form. THE CHANGE. A new `_breakBorrowed(d)` predicate modelled line-for-line on `_breakPreserved` - defensive null checks, one try/catch, returns false on anything it cannot read - added immediately above `_breakBegin`, then applied in the same two places `_breakPreserved` is: the filter, and the `_breakDie` gate. Its seat test (`G.matchDice[ft.lane]===ft.borrowed`) is deliberately the same test startPTurn's loan-expiry block already runs at 22968, so the two can never disagree about whether the loan is still standing in its lane.

WHICH CALLERS STILL REACH `_removeDieAt`'s FAIR-TRADE BRANCH. Two callers exist in the file: `_breakDie` (17898, `_removeDieAt(lane,{permanent:true})`) and the Obsidian shatter sweep in afterRoll (23709, `_shLanes.forEach(function(L){_removeDieAt(L,{permanent:false});})`). After this patch `_breakDie` can never arrive with a lane that holds a live loan, so the branch is DEAD FOR BREAK and STILL LIVE FOR NATURAL SHATTER - which is precisely the path the brief says is unchanged. The branch's code is therefore untouched; only its leading comment is rewritten, because that comment currently justifies itself entirely in terms of what breaking a borrowed die costs, which is now impossible, and a cold reader would otherwise read the struck 4b ruling as current and could "restore" it to Break. Nothing else in the branch (`_ftDead` recording, the owner walking back into the lane, the pool filter, the famLog, `saveMatchState`) changes.

No UI, save-shape, or card-text change is needed: `_breakBegin` already returns false on an empty list and both call sites (23403 and 25077) handle that.

1. EMPTY TARGET LIST IS REACHABLE AND IS ALREADY HANDLED, BUT THE PLAYER PAYS FOR NOTHING. If the only other free die is the borrowed one, `live.length===0`, `_breakBegin` famLogs NOTHING LEFT TO BREAK and returns false. Both callers cope: the roll path (23403) falls through and the turn carries on; the bank path (25077) clears `G._breakThenBank` and banks. No dead buttons, because `setBtns(false,false)` runs only after the empty check. So the UI does not lock - I verified the ordering. What the player loses is the Break itself (the skull/300g charge is already spent when `_breakPending` was armed), with only a log line to explain it. That failure mode pre-exists for preserved and all-committed hands; this ruling makes it reachable more often, and it is worth a design decision on whether a fizzled Break should refund. Not fixed here - out of scope of this ruling.

2. THE STRUCK 4b RULING IS STILL LIVE ON THE NATURAL-SHATTER PATH, AND THE BRIEF IS AMBIGUOUS ABOUT WHETHER IT SHOULD BE. Section 1 says natural shatter "still follows the existing ruling above (the player loses the die they lent, gone until next match, exactly as if it died at home)". Section 2's ruling is about the LENT die's fate and says nothing about seat count; section 4b's lane-persists ruling - struck, but struck in the context of Break - is what actually keeps the player at 6. Read literally, "exactly as if it died at home" would leave the player at 5 dice, which is NOT what `_removeDieAt` does today. I have left the branch behaviourally untouched because the task and the brief both say natural shatter is UNCHANGED, but if the intent is that a natural shatter on a borrowed die should also cost a seat, that is a second, separate ruling and this patch does not make it. Flagging rather than guessing.

3. THE SEAT TEST IS A JUDGEMENT CALL. `_breakPreserved` tests lane alone; `_breakBorrowed` tests lane AND that `matchDice[ft.lane]` still equals `ft.borrowed`. I chose the stricter test to agree with startPTurn's expiry block, but it means that if another effect overwrites that seat mid-loan (steal_die at 23120, the mirror-match swaps at 23088/27433/29302, `G.matchDice[...]=newMat` at 29747) the die now standing there becomes a legal Break target. I believe that is correct - it is not the borrowed die - but if the ruling meant "the LANE is protected while a loan is live", drop the `matchDice` comparison and keep only the `_laneOf(d)!==ft.lane` test. One-line change either way.

4. `_laneOf`'s FALLBACK. For a die with no `lane` stamp it returns the pool INDEX, which can coincidentally equal `ft.lane` and wrongly protect an unrelated die, or miss a real one. Every die the game builds is stamped, and `_breakPreserved` carries the identical exposure, so this adds no new class of bug - but it is the one way the predicate can be wrong.

5. THE `_breakDie` GATE IS UNREACHABLE THROUGH THE UI, DELIBERATELY. `_breakBegin` binds `_breakDie` only to dice it offered and does not strip `toggleDie` from the rest, so tapping a borrowed die during targeting will TOGGLE-SELECT it rather than log the new message. That is exactly how a preserved die already behaves; if the ruling wants a visible refusal on tap, the fix is in `_breakBegin`'s non-target handling and applies to both predicates at once. Out of scope here, but do not expect to see the new famLog in normal play.

6. `G._fairTrade.lane` IS MUTABLE MID-TURN. `_removeDieAt` decrements it when a lower seat is destroyed (17823). The predicate reads it live on every call rather than caching, so it stays correct across a removal inside the same targeting session - but a second Break armed in the same turn after a removal depends on that decrement being right, which is pre-existing code I did not change.
